title: Campus Cash
html:
Campus Cash

Spent this month $0.00

explanations.title: Total card
explanations.what_it_does: Shows how much has been spent in total. It updates every time an expense is added or deleted.
explanations.how_it_works: `totalSpent()` walks through `state.expenses` and adds up every `amount` using `reduce`. `renderTotal()` then formats that number with `toFixed(2)` and writes it into the `<strong id="total">` element.
explanations.concept_note: The total isn't stored anywhere. It is calculated from the list each time, so it can never get out of sync with the data.
explanations.try_changing: Change `.toFixed(2)` to `.toFixed(0)` in `renderTotal()` and the total will round to whole dollars.

explanations.title: Amount field
explanations.what_it_does: Where you type how much you spent. Anything that isn't a positive number gets a red border when you press Add.
explanations.how_it_works: `readAmount()` reads the field with `parseFloat`, then returns the number only if `Number.isFinite(value) && value > 0`. Otherwise it returns `null`, which the Add button treats as invalid input.
explanations.concept_note: Never trust what a user typed. Check it before it goes into your data.
explanations.try_changing: Change `value > 0` to `value >= 0`, then try adding an expense of 0 to see it accepted.

explanations.title: Category dropdown
explanations.what_it_does: Lets you pick which category a new expense belongs to.
explanations.how_it_works: The `<select>` starts empty. This code loops over the `CATEGORIES` array with `map`, turns each name into an `<option>` string, joins them together and assigns the result to `innerHTML`.
explanations.concept_note: Keep the data in one array and let code build the HTML from it. Change the array and the interface follows.
explanations.try_changing: Add `"Coffee"` to the `CATEGORIES` array at the top of the script. A new dropdown option and a new filter chip appear.

explanations.title: Add expense button
explanations.what_it_does: Adds the expense you typed to the top of the list and clears the form.
explanations.how_it_works: The click handler calls `readAmount()`. If it returns `null` it marks the field invalid and stops. Otherwise it builds a new expense object, creates a new array with it at the front (`[newItem, ...state.expenses]`), clears the inputs and calls `render()` to redraw the screen.
explanations.concept_note: A user action changes the data first, then the screen is redrawn from that data. The interface never edits itself directly.
explanations.try_changing: Rewrite the array as `[...state.expenses, { ... }]`, with the spread first, so new expenses land at the bottom of the list.

explanations.title: Category filter chips
explanations.what_it_does: A row of buttons that narrows the list down to one category.
explanations.how_it_works: Clicking a chip stores its category in `state.filter` and calls `render()`. `visibleExpenses()` then uses `filter` to keep only the expenses whose `category` matches. The listener sits on the container and uses `closest('[data-filter]')` to find which chip was clicked.
explanations.concept_note: `filter` returns a new array containing only the items that pass a test, and leaves the original untouched.
explanations.try_changing: In `visibleExpenses()`, change `e.category === state.filter` to `e.category !== state.filter`. Each chip will now show everything except its own category.

explanations.title: Expense list
explanations.what_it_does: The scrolling list of expenses, or a short message when there is nothing to show.
explanations.how_it_works: `renderList()` takes the visible expenses, turns each one into an `<li>` with a template string using `map`, joins them into one string and sets `listEl.innerHTML`. If the array is empty it shows the empty message instead.
explanations.concept_note: The screen is a function of the data: whatever is in the array is what gets drawn, so you never add or remove list items by hand.
explanations.try_changing: Swap the `.name` and `.cat` text inside the `<li>` template. Every row flips at once, because they all come from the same template.

explanations.title: Delete button
explanations.what_it_does: Removes that one expense from the list.
explanations.how_it_works: Instead of attaching a listener to every ✕ button, one listener on the whole list catches every click. `closest('[data-delete]')` finds which button was pressed, its `data-delete` value is the expense id, and `filter` builds a new array without that item before `render()` redraws.
explanations.concept_note: Attach one listener to a parent and let clicks bubble up to it. It keeps working for buttons that are created later.
explanations.try_changing: Change `e.id !== id` to `e.id === id`. Deleting an expense will now remove everything except the one you clicked.
